English: Boat Builders Shed
A humble wooden shed by the water, sheltering a handful of craftsmen assembling small fishing boats and ferries. The first spark of maritime industry.
Timber Drydock
A makeshift drydock of timber and earthworks, allowing more ambitious ship repairs and the assembly of larger hulls for coastal trade.
Log Slipway
A simple log slipway extends into the water, enabling the construction and launching of modest riverboats and small merchant vessels.
Shipwrights Yard
A bustling yard with workshops and timber stockpiles, employing skilled carpenters for the construction of merchant cogs and sturdy warships.
Mariners' Guild
A prestigious guildhall where shipmasters and navigators gather, regulating trade, training sailors, and strengthening the citys maritime influence.
Carvel Workshop
Large covered slipways and specialized workshops for advanced carvel-built hulls, increasing the ports shipbuilding capacity and prestige.
Boat Basin
A fortified basin carved from the riverbank, providing safe mooring for both merchant and military ships, drawing bustling trade to the city.
Dockside Crane
A massive wooden treadwheel crane dominates the docks, facilitating rapid loading and unloading of cargo, and greatly expanding trade volume.
Naval Warehouse
Expansive stone warehouses line the waterfront, securing goods and naval stores, supporting both commerce and city defense.
Grand Shipyard
A sprawling complex of stone and steel, the Grand Shipyard is the envy of kingdoms, launching fleets and commanding the seas with unmatched economic might.
